newsitem.title: UK: Survey shows Britons ignorant about cancer.
newsitem.headline: Survey shows Britons ignorant about cancer.

text.p: Nearly half of the British public does not associate smoking with cancer, while seven out of eight do not know sunbathing can cause cancer, charity researchers reported on Tuesday.

The survey, conducted by pollsters NOP for the Macmillan Cancer Relief Fund, found "a disturbing lack of awareness" about how widespread cancer is. Cancer is the second-biggest killer, after heart disease, in industrialised countries.

"Despite nine out of 10 people knowing someone who has cancer and nearly a quarter of the population knowing an astonishing 10 or more people, almost half the people surveyed thought they were unlikely to develop cancer themselves," Macmillan said in a statement.
"In fact, one in three people will develop skin cancer at some point in their life."
Of the 1,000 adults surveyed by NOP, only 12 percent knew that sunbathing could cause skin cancer. Between 49 and 67 percent, depending on the region, knew smoking caused cancer.

Those surveyed came up with some unusual fears, Macmillan added. "Despite no proven links, bad hygiene, exercise, microwaves, physical injuries and chewing gum were named as causes of cancer," it said.
